subject: Renewal uplift & co-term path for InsightHealth
messages:
From: Lara Chen <lara.chen@insighthealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@insighthealth.com
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal uplift + mid-contract add-on — options and timeline

Hi Marcus / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We’re seeing a faster-than-expected production ramp on our clinical summarization feature and need to lock in a path for a mid-contract uplift. Two asks from our side:

1) Add 30% more dedicated capacity for the next 6 months (we’ll likely sustain a portion after renewal).
2) Co-term the uplift with our Feb 2027 renewal so procurement is simpler.

Can you outline the pricing options (annualize vs. temporary top-up), potential discounting for committed uplift, and what legal/ops steps we need to finish before the end of October? Procurement asked for a mutual action plan they can attach to the PO.

Appreciate a short summary and an MRP (mutual action plan) doc if possible.

Best,
Lara
Lara Chen
Head of Product Operations
InsightHealth

--
Attachments: none
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@insighthealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal uplift + mid-contract add-on — options and timeline

Hi Lara,

Thanks — this is good context. Short answer: we can support both a temporary top-up and an annualized uplift that co-terms to Feb 2027. High-level options below (pricing ballpark included for context):

Option A — Temporary surge (6 months)
- Add 30% dedicated units for 6 months only.
- Rate: standard hosted top-up rate (no committed discount) — estimated $X/month (see pricing file).
- Legal: simple amendment; PO + updated MSA appendix; ops can provision within 7 business days once PO’s accepted.

Option B — Annualize & co-term to Feb 2027 (preferred for cost predictability)
- Convert uplift to committed annualized units that end on your renewal date.
- Effective discount tiers: 10% for +25% commit, 18% for +40% commit, 22% for +60% commit (examples; final depends on total commitment and billing cadence).
- Billing: pro-rate remainder of current term and then annual billing aligned to Feb 2027.
- Legal: amendment + SOW amendment; estimated 3-week review for standard customers.

Option C — Blended voucher + top-up (intermediate)
- Issue vouchers that cover a portion of uplift cost for 6 months, convert remaining to annual committed units at renewal. Vouchers give you runway today and predictability at renewal.

Operational notes & timeline
- We can prepare a Mutual Action Plan template today and a pricing v2 spreadsheet (attached).
- To meet end-of-October operational readiness we need: signed PO (procurement), confirmed billing cadence (InsightHealth AP), and a legal point-of-contact for the amendment.

Next steps I suggest:
- I’ll attach a draft MAP and the updated pricing workbook for your review.
- Kimberly — can you confirm the max discount band we can offer pre-approval (we typically need exec approval for >15%)?
- Lara — if you can share the expected average monthly token/embedding volume after the 30% increase, we’ll produce a firm quote.

Thanks,
Marcus
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal uplift + mid-contract add-on — options and timeline

Thanks Marcus and Lara — attaching quick notes.

Pricing guardrails:
- Standard practice: up to 15% off list for mid-term top-ups (rep-approved).
- Discounts beyond 15% require manager/exec sign-off; for cases where we annualize commitments we can stretch to 18–20% with a smaller headroom if there’s expansion potential and multi-year renewal.

Operationally:
- If InsightHealth wants co-term to Feb 2027 and annualize, we should target the +40% commit band to justify a larger discount (18%).
- If they only want a 6-month surge, voucher+top-up is usually cleaner for bookkeeping.

Neha — can you confirm if Finance is comfortable approving a one-off 18% discount if we lock in a Feb 2027 annualized commit and include a minimum uplift renewal guarantee?

Kimberly Park
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal uplift + mid-contract add-on — options and timeline

Quick note from Finance/Ops:

- We can approve up to an 18% discount on an annualized co-term if commercial includes: (a) signed amendment committing to the uplift units through Feb 2027, (b) a minimum spend protection clause (to avoid material churn risk), and (c) agreement to case escalation SLAs.
- We require revenue recognition clarity on the pro-rated portion; ask AP to confirm billing cadence (net 30 vs net 45).
- Exec approval required for anything >18% or multi-year payment deferrals.

Please include a brief commercial rationale in the MAP (expected ARR lift, retention lift estimate) so I can expedite the sign-off.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
